summary: Do not append the current skeletons: missing inputs, leaked answer images, truncated keys, damaged cases and collapsed tables require parser/post-process fixes.
report:
BLOCKER
- Missing student inputs ? 1-3, Savvas Try It 3(b); 1-4-savvas-q17; 2-3-savvas-q42. The post-process deletes every placeholder after the FIRST answer. Try It 3(b) consequently has only "b." and a FIG comment; q17 loses the only day-1/day-5 distances (2 and 3.2 miles); q42 loses the only garden dimensions (9 by 14 m). Five student input illustrations were removed in total: these three essential inputs plus 1-4 q26 and q35 (their equivalent information survives in text/table). Evidence: a2_1-3_TE.tex:333, a2_1-4_TE.tex:683, a2_2-3_TE.tex:704; te_postprocess.py:34. Fix: replace the first-answer/tail heuristic with placeholder roles tied to source figure and question part; preserve input figures regardless of position. Regenerate from TeX, since editing the already-stripped output cannot restore inputs.

- Answer images remain in SIX student rows ? Model & Discuss launches in 1-3 (two completed graphs), 2-1 (completed doubled-area graph), and 2-7 (sample sketch/intersections); 1-3 Try It 5 (completed parking step graph despite "Graph the function"); 2-1-savvas-q21; 2-7 Try It 4. The last two still expose raw \placeholder{graph}{...answer...} commands, including the complete solution graph. The post-process covers only Practice/Try It, assumes answers follow \answer{}, and cannot match nested-brace descriptions. Fix: balanced parsing of both placeholder arguments, then role-based exclusion before text conversion across ALL student environments. Keep answer descriptions in notes. Explicit source-figure role overrides in the post-process can handle ambiguous figures without hand-editing skeletons.

- Answer keys truncated ? ALL nine lessons; 34 student rows lose 64 subsequent \answer{} blocks. extract_answer at ingest_lesson_from_latex.py:265 uses next(...), while prompt cleanup removes every answer. Affected: 1-3 launch, Try Its 2/3, q23; 1-4 launch, q17/26/34/35/38; 2-1 launch, Try Its 1/5, q15/38; 2-2 launch, q26/27/30; 2-3 launch, q41/42/45; 2-4 launch, q46/47/48/50; 2-5 launch, q50/54; 2-6 launch, q37; 2-7 launch. For example, 1-4 q35 notes retain only part a, losing recursive definition, 63 push-ups, and 648 total; 2-6 q37 notes contain only "Yes" for five equations. Fix: collect ALL balanced answer blocks in order, preserving part/table-row labels and repeated values; do not deduplicate "Yes"/"No" or R/I/C answers. Teacher-reference rows also exhibit this defect.

- Piecewise definitions damaged ? 41 skeleton rows (1-3: 28; 1-4: 13), including 23 student rows with damage in prompts and/or keys. Student rows: 1-3 Try Its 2/3/4 and q12/13/15/16/17/18/19/20/22/23/24/25/27; 1-4 Try Its 2/3 and q12/22/23/24/25. Example: 1-3-savvas-q13 turns the TeX row boundary into "7,&x>3 5x-3,&x?3", merging condition and next expression. DROP_COMMANDS removes \\ before environments are processed (ingest_lesson_from_latex.py:97,208). Fix: protect/convert cases before generic command stripping, retaining separate expression/condition pairs in both prompt and notes.

- Table row boundaries lost ? 18 skeleton rows have fewer output table rows than their TeX tables (including three student rows: 2-1-savvas-q36, 2-4-savvas-q48, 2-6-savvas-q37). q36's six transformations become one pipe-separated line; q48's seven unanswered numbers become one row; q37's five equations become one row and lose their response cells. Counts by lesson: 1-3=1, 1-4=2, 2-1=3, 2-2=3, 2-3=1, 2-4=4, 2-5=0, 2-6=3, 2-7=1. No literal [TABLE] replacements were found. Fix: parse tabular BEFORE deleting \\; preserve empty cells instead of filtering them in simplify_tabular (line 227). This also fixes the shifted blank header cell in 1-4-savvas-q36. Newlines happen to preserve many other tables but are not reliable row delimiters.

- Figure descriptions disclose requested equations ? at least 2-1-savvas-q13, 2-1-savvas-q29, and 2-3-savvas-q12 ask students to derive the equation, while their [IMAGE: ...] text explicitly supplies respectively y=-2(x+3)^2+4, y=2(x+1)^2-6, and y=(x+1)(x+6). This is inherited from the TeX figure descriptions, not newly invented by ingestion. Keep reconstruction equations in figure metadata/notes and emit student-safe figure text or the actual student graph; do not publish rendering instructions as question text.

FIX
- Math conversion ? 35 rows retain \frac commands in prompts/notes (1-4=13, 2-2=1, 2-6=19, 2-7=2), including 13 student rows. Unbraced fractions such as 1-4 q24's \frac18 and q30's \frac n2 are never converted; fractions containing radicals, e.g. 2-6 q38's \frac{1??(...)}{2(2)}, remain mixed LaTeX/plain text because fraction processing precedes radical conversion. Also, SIX 1-4 rows turn \cdots into "?s", including Try It 6 ("8+13+18+?s+43"), Examples 5/6, Concept Box, ElicitEvidence for Example 6, and Assess ELLAddendum. Fix: tokenize complete command names/arguments (including single-token arguments), process nested fraction/radical expressions to completion, and handle \cdots before \cdot with command boundaries. No matrix/array environments were present.

- Placeholder/visual metadata ? SIX rows retain raw \placeholder commands; four are student rows: 2-1 q21; 2-7 Try It 4, q24, q29. Nested braces defeat strip_placeholders' flat regex (line 157), so descriptions also fail to enter IMAGE PLACEHOLDER notes. Separately, 61 rows containing [IMAGE:] report has_visual=false, including 17 student rows; e.g. 1-3 q17 and 2-1 q13. detect_visual_type (line 248) has no graph-placeholder branch. Fix: balanced placeholder parsing and compute visual metadata from retained STUDENT figures after cleanup. The false graph flag is also present in accepted lesson 1-2.

- Exact calibration exception ? 2-5, item_analysis.example_5.dok1 omits 52. TeX line 533 explicitly contains "43--48, \te{52}", and its annotation says the printed table associates 52 with BOTH Examples 3 and 5; calibration retains only Example 3. This is deliberate source annotation/parser suppression, not an unexplained DOK error. To meet the requested exact Example?DOK map, preserve that numeric association within item-analysis parsing and allow multiple example associations; a single skeleton anchor need not erase calibration evidence. Item 53 is absent from the printed table but has its practice row.

- Standalone context ? 1-3 Try It 1 asks Alani's pay without the rate from Example 1; 2-6 Try It 4 refers to Rachel's serve without its model from Example 4. These faithfully reproduce their TeX blocks but need linked example context or automatically inherited givens before standalone student use.

- Transcription comments ? 36 rows, including 16 student rows, expose % FIG coordinates. Strip unescaped TeX comments from student text while retaining figure provenance separately.

NOTE
- Reviewed 713 skeleton rows, including 326 student rows and all 268 practice declarations. Every practice has exactly one matching row with the declared DOK. All nine Lesson Quiz DOK maps and skills-review maps match their TeX tables (five items per lesson). Example?DOK maps match in eight lessons; the sole exception is the documented 2-5 association above.
- All lettered multiple-choice options and multipart question wording survive the source-to-output comparison; the material losses are the missing images, answer keys, and table structure identified above. No residual \te{} or \answer{} commands were found in student prompts.
- Accepted lesson 1-2 uses the same row/tag structure and already shows first-answer-only notes and false graph flags. Its acceptance does not establish that these behaviors meet this review's explicit completeness requirements.
- Tagged teacher-edition addenda, teacher-reference Examples, and reference concept rows were not treated as student questions or flagged simply for containing instructional solutions. Error-analysis and critique prompts legitimately include proposed student work.
- Review was read-only apart from the requested result JSON. No git, append, ingest-main, or post-process mutation commands were run. Checks used independent table/DOK comparisons plus in-memory parser calls under python -B. GitNexus MCP was unavailable; no symbols were edited.

YELLOW ? append after the listed content and parser fixes, regeneration, and re-review.
